Lamb's Lettuce Salad

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4 as a sidePrep 15 min

This delicate Lamb's Lettuce Salad, also known as Mâche, is a wonderful way to celebrate Candlemas, the Feast of the Presentation, which traditionally marks the midpoint of winter and the anticipation of spring. Its tender, slightly nutty leaves are among the first greens to emerge, symbolizing new life and the approaching warmth, making it a perfect fresh counterpoint to heartier winter fare.

Ingredients

  • 5 ounces (140 g) fresh lamb's lettuce (mâche)
  • 3 tablespoons (45 ml) extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) white wine vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 1/8 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • Optional: 1 small shallot, finely minced

Method

  1. Gently wash the lamb's lettuce under cool running water, ensuring all grit is removed.
  2. Carefully dry the lettuce using a salad spinner or by patting it very gently with paper towels. It is crucial for the lettuce to be thoroughly dry for the dressing to adhere properly.
  3. In a small bowl, whisk together the extra virgin olive oil, white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until well combined and emulsified.
  4. If using, stir the finely minced shallot into the dressing mixture.
  5. Place the dried lamb's lettuce in a large salad bowl.
  6. Just before serving, pour the prepared dressing over the lettuce.
  7. Toss gently to coat all the delicate leaves evenly.
  8. Serve immediately to enjoy the crisp texture and fresh flavor.

Tips

  • For added texture and a complementary flavor, sprinkle the salad with a few toasted walnuts or pecans.
  • A touch of crumbled goat cheese or feta can also enhance the delicate taste of the mâche.
  • Always dress lamb's lettuce just before serving, as its tender leaves can wilt quickly once combined with dressing.
